bites.title: Reading papers and model release notes
bites.body:
Reading technical papers and official model release notes is how a professional AI consultant gets primary facts instead of relying on distorted social media threads. Model system cards and release notes tell you the exact context window, knowledge cutoff, pricing, tool-calling changes, safety evaluations, and known failure modes directly from the lab that built the model.

It is like a pharmacist reading the official clinical trial summary and prescribing sheet for a new medicine rather than trusting a thirty-second television advert.

When skimming a paper or system card, focus first on the evaluation methodology, the baseline comparisons, and the limitations section to see where the technique actually breaks down.
bites.sourceNote: Drafted by AI, November 2026 · confidence: high

questions.prompt: Where should an AI consultant look first inside a new model's official release notes or system card?

choices.text: The graphic design credits and font choices on the cover page
The evaluation methodology, baseline comparisons, pricing/latency specs, and documented limitations or failure modes
Anonymous comments posted by social media influencers before trying the model
Only the single highest benchmark number highlighted in the marketing headline

questions.explanation: Primary technical documentation and limitation sections reveal how the model was actually tested, what changed from prior versions, and where it still struggles in real workflows.

bites.title: Building a personal research workflow
bites.body:
Building a personal research workflow keeps you informed about real AI advances without drowning in daily noise or burning out. Instead of doom-scrolling news feeds all day, curate a small list of high-signal primary sources such as official lab blogs, key framework changelogs, and one or two trusted technical digests, and block a dedicated sixty-minute slot each week to test one new capability hands-on.

It is like a chef visiting the wholesale market once a week to taste seasonal ingredients in person rather than reading restaurant gossip columns every ten minutes while trying to cook service.

Hands-on experiments with your own small benchmark tasks teach you more in an hour than reading fifty opinion posts.
bites.sourceNote: Drafted by AI, November 2026 · confidence: high

questions.prompt: What is the most effective habit for an AI consultant to stay current without getting overwhelmed by daily announcements?

choices.text: Read every single AI post on social media twenty-four hours a day and rewrite client code daily
Ignore all new model releases for five years at a time to avoid distraction
Follow a small set of primary technical sources and dedicate a regular weekly slot to hands-on testing with your own practical evaluation tasks
Adopt every new open-source library in client production systems the morning it is announced

questions.explanation: Combining curated primary sources with scheduled hands-on testing against your own benchmark tasks separates genuinely useful capabilities from daily noise.

bites.title: Re-testing your system when a new model arrives
bites.body:
Whenever a model provider releases a new frontier or fast model, or deprecates an older snapshot, you should run your project's automated evaluation and security regression suite against the new candidate before switching production traffic. A newer model frequently lets you simplify complex multi-step chains, drop brittle prompt workarounds, or cut token costs in half, but it can also change formatting habits or verbosity in ways that break downstream parsers.

Think of a racing team bolting a newer engine onto their car: they always run telemetry laps on the test track first to tune the gearbox before entering Sunday's race.

With a good eval suite already in place, testing a brand-new model takes an afternoon rather than a month of guesswork.
bites.sourceNote: Drafted by AI, November 2026 · confidence: high

questions.prompt: Why should you run your automated evaluation suite whenever a new model version is released, even if the new model tops public leaderboards?

choices.text: Because public leaderboards are written in encrypted code that nobody can read
Because new models always perform worse than three-year-old models on every task
Because cloud providers delete your database if you do not run an eval within one hour of a release
To verify that the new model improves cost, latency, or quality on your specific client tasks without breaking custom formatting, tool calls, or safety guardrails

questions.explanation: Even when a new model is stronger overall, subtle shifts in instruction following, verbosity, or tool-call formatting can either unlock simpler architectures or break assumptions in your existing pipeline.

bites.title: Telling real progress from hype
bites.body:
Telling real progress from hype is one of the highest-value skills an AI consultant brings to executive clients who are bombarded by vendor sales pitches every day. When evaluating a flashy demo or product claim, always ask to see performance on messy out-of-distribution data, end-to-end latency and cost per successful task, failure handling when tools error out, and independent benchmarks rather than cherry-picked examples.

Anyone can record a slick two-minute video of an agent booking a flight on the tenth try after hiding the nine failed takes that booked the wrong airport.

Real engineering progress shows up as higher reliability on your client's own evaluation dataset at a lower total cost of ownership.
bites.sourceNote: Drafted by AI, November 2026 · confidence: high

questions.prompt: What is the best way to tell whether a vendor's flashy AI agent demo represents real production readiness or marketing hype?

choices.text: Count how many views and likes the demo video received on social media
Check whether the vendor's website uses futuristic animations and buzzwords
Ask the salesperson whether their product is powered by artificial general intelligence
Test the system on your client's own messy edge-case data while measuring end-to-end success rate, failure recovery, latency, and cost per completed task

questions.explanation: Flashy demos often rely on cherry-picked inputs and hidden retries; testing against your own representative dataset and measuring reliability, latency, and cost exposes how the system actually performs.
